column2: I taught myself, and I have come this far.
The sound of the British Empire, for your orchestra.
A self-taught composer who shot to fame at 42 with the Enigma Variations.
Minuet in G
After the piano, my homeland: Poland.
I promise you a full house.
A superstar pianist. He later became prime minister of independent Poland.
At the tip of the baton, music turns to magic.
If you can share me with the Gewandhaus.

Conductor of both the Gewandhaus and the Berlin Philharmonic. In 1913 he recorded Beethoven's Fifth complete with the Berlin Philharmonic, regarded as a pioneering complete symphony recording by a great orchestra and a great conductor.
Beethoven: Piano Concerto 'Emperor'
I have just won a competition, as it happens.
With a touch of steel, I shall hold up your orchestra.
In 1905 he won the piano prize at the Rubinstein Competition in Paris. Second place went to Bartók.
Bach–Busoni: Chaconne
The music of the future has yet to be written by anyone.
I shall lend you my strength, pupils and all.
Famous for his Bach transcriptions. His Sketch of a New Aesthetic of Music (1907) foretold the music of the future.
Verdi: Otello
Come è scritto! As written!
With a single baton I shall knock your orchestra into shape.
In 1887 he played the cello in the premiere of Otello. Known for conducting from memory and for his temper; snapped batons were an everyday matter.
'Un bel dì vedremo' from Madama Butterfly
I have bought a new motor car. Shall I give you a ride?
If it is melodies that bring tears you want, leave them to me.
The 1904 premiere of Madama Butterfly at La Scala was a fiasco; the revised version was a triumph. He loved motor cars and hunting.
Piano Concerto No. 2
Very well.

Savaged at the premiere of his First Symphony, he long laid down his pen, but made a brilliant return with the Second Piano Concerto (1901). His hands were so large they are said to have spanned a thirteenth.
Le Poème de l'extase
This chord looks violet, does it not?
With colour and sound, let us set the cosmos ringing.
A synaesthete who saw colours in sounds; his Prometheus (1910) has a part for a 'colour keyboard'.
Double Bass Concerto
I shall make the double bass sing for you.
My means and my publishing house are at your service.
A double-bass virtuoso. With his wife's fortune he founded a publishing house and an orchestra, and later became a celebrated conductor of the Boston Symphony Orchestra.
Ballet: The Rite of Spring
Rhythm is the backbone of music.
With primal rhythm, let us shake the world.
On 29 May 1913, at the Paris premiere of The Rite of Spring, the shouting and brawling in the house all but drowned the music.
Violin Concerto (revised version, 1905)
In the woods at Ainola, I hear symphonies.
I shall bring you the sound of the North.
He lived at Ainola, outside Helsinki. Debts troubled him again and again.
Romanian Folk Dances
I go from village to village recording the songs of the old people.
The power of folk song, for your orchestra.
He lost to Backhaus at the 1905 Rubinstein Competition. That same year he began collecting folk songs with Kodály.
Bach: Goldberg Variations (harpsichord)
Bach should be played on the harpsichord.
Let us bring the sound of the harpsichord back to life.
The driving force of the harpsichord revival. She had Pleyel build harpsichords to her order.
Sonata for solo violin
I have come from Brussels.
I shall lend you the bow of the Belgian school.
He gave the premiere of Debussy's String Quartet. Franck's Violin Sonata was a wedding present to him.

Premiere of a new tone poem
Premiere of the St John Passion

First performed on Good Friday at the Nikolaikirche. The town council frowned: 'too theatrical'.

Fame +30
The Concert Spirituel has been founded in Paris: the beginning of public concerts, held on days when religious observance closes the theatres.
Vivaldi's concerto collection Il cimento dell'armonia e dell'inventione has been published. Its first four concertos are The Four Seasons.
Faustina has arrived in London. The 'war of the divas' with Cuzzoni begins.
Premiere of the St Matthew Passion

Believed to have been first performed on Good Friday at the Thomaskirche. This great work will lie forgotten until Mendelssohn revives it some 100 years later.

Fame +50
The war of the divas: uproar in the house

On 6 June, during an opera by Bononcini and in the presence of the Princess of Wales, the partisans of Faustina and of Cuzzoni began trading catcalls and whistles, and the performance was broken off.
The story that the two pulled each other's hair on stage is thought to be a fabrication spread by the satires of the day.
Both are in your orchestra! Their satisfaction has plummeted.
Coronation of George II

You composed the coronation anthem 'Zadok the Priest'. It will be sung at every British coronation from now on.

Fame +40
The Beggar's Opera craze

The Beggar's Opera, the English ballad opera by John Gay and Pepusch, is a smash hit. Italian opera is laughed at as out of date, and the Royal Academy of Music totters. It was said to have 'made Gay rich and Rich gay'.
A heavy blow to your company (-3,000 fr)
Collegium Musicum

You took over the direction of the Collegium Musicum, a students' music society. Weekly concerts are held at Zimmermann's coffee house.

+250 fr every month
A memorandum to the town council
Bach submitted his 'Short but most necessary draft for a well-appointed church music' to the council, complaining of the shortage of players. …The council turned a deaf ear.
The 'Affaire Ravel' in Paris. The judging of the Prix de Rome came under fire and the director of the Conservatoire resigned. Fauré succeeded him.
Premiere of Debussy's La Mer. The cover of the score shows Hokusai's 'Great Wave off Kanagawa'.
Premiere of Salome

First performed at the Dresden Court Opera, with 38 curtain calls. Kaiser Wilhelm II said, 'This will do him harm' — and Strauss retorted that the harm had built him a villa in Garmisch.

Fame +60
R. Strauss's Salome was first performed in Dresden, to great success.
Leaving the Court Opera

Worn down by antisemitic attacks and intrigue, Mahler resigned as director of the Vienna Court Opera.

The monthly salary has ended.
Mahler has resigned from the Vienna Court Opera and sailed for New York. Vienna is open!
An invitation from the New World
The Metropolitan Opera in New York has invited you as a conductor.
Accept<small>New York comes under your control</small>
Took the Metropolitan Opera.
Diaghilev's Ballets Russes has opened in Paris. The taste of Paris changed overnight.
Premiere of The Firebird. The unknown Stravinsky became famous in a single night.
Premiere of the 'Symphony of a Thousand'

Symphony No. 8 was first performed in Munich. More than 1,000 performers took part, and notables such as Thomas Mann crowded in. The greatest success of Mahler's life.

Fame +80
Premiere of Der Rosenkavalier

First performed in Dresden. Special trains known as 'Rosenkavalier trains' were laid on from Berlin.

Fame +60
Premiere of Der Rosenkavalier — such a sensation that special trains ran from Berlin.
Uproar at the premiere of The Rite of Spring
29 May, Théâtre des Champs-Élysées. From the high bassoon of the opening the audience grew restless, and soon came shouting and brawling. The dancers could not hear the orchestra.
Use the scandal as publicity<small>fame +80, but funds -1,000</small>
Try to calm things down<small>fame +20</small>
Premiere of The Rite of Spring. The Théâtre des Champs-Élysées was engulfed in shouting and brawling.
Leipzig, 1723

You have taken up the post of Kantor at the Thomaskirche. But the town council's opinion of you is cool.
During the selection, Councillor Platz is recorded as saying: 'Since the best cannot be had, we must make do with the middling.'
London, 1723

As music director of the Royal Academy of Music you lead the Italian opera venture. Your star singers are as strong-willed as they are gifted.
The Royal Academy of Music was not today's conservatoire but an opera company financed by the nobility.

Records, the telephone, the Atlantic liners: a new century in which the market for music suddenly widens.
The Metropolitan Opera in New York lies three months away by ship. The great star Caruso is waiting.
Pièces de viole: 'Le Tableau de l'opération de la taille'
On the viol I shall paint you an operation, step by step.
Let me lend you the hand that served His Majesty Louis XIV.

The great master of the viola da gamba. His 'Tableau de l'opération de la taille' of 1725 is a curiosity that depicts the terrors of surgery in sound. He is also the hero of the film Tous les matins du monde.
Symphonies pour les Soupers du Roy
It is the hour of His Majesty's supper, so let us be brief.
The sound of Versailles, for your orchestra.
Master of the Chapel Royal under Louis XIV and Louis XV. He wrote suites to be played while the King dined.
Opéra-ballet: L'Europe galante
The sun of the Midi, on the stages of Paris.
With song and dance, I shall set the house alight.
He established the 'opéra-ballet', fusing opera and ballet. Born in Aix-en-Provence, he brought with him a cheerful Italian taste.
Concertos for five flutes
Write it and it sells. That is my way.
Let us split the takings from the scores.
One of the first composers to make a fortune from publishing his music. Teased that he effortlessly 'brought forth a volume every month', he is said to have replied: 'I am earning money.'
Violin sonatas
I began as a ballet dancer, you know. In bowing, too, footwork is everything.
I shall lend you the bow of the French violin school.
Founder of the French violin school. Originally a ballet dancer, he made his debut at the Concert Spirituel in 1728.
Lully: Armide
I am not in the mood tonight.
For your stage, I shall not fail to appear.
A great soprano of the Paris Opéra. Capricious, she was once imprisoned for failing to appear.
Harpsichord piece 'Le Coucou'
At the age of six I played before His Majesty Louis XIV.
For improvisation at the organ, look no further.
A keyboard player famed as a child prodigy. In 1727 he competed with Rameau for the post of organist at Saint-Paul and won.
Marais: 'Le Tableau de l'opération de la taille'
Harpsichord (with narration)
Delalande: Symphonies pour les Soupers du Roy
Campra: L'Europe galante
Singer
Boismortier: Concertos for five flutes
Rameau: 'La Poule'
Daquin: 'Le Coucou'
Opéra-comique: Richard Cœur-de-lion
The Queen is waiting for my new work.
The laughter and tears of opéra-comique, for your stage.
The Belgian-born king of opéra-comique. A favourite of Queen Marie Antoinette.
Symphony in D major
France has symphonies too, you know.
I shall take on the task of holding the orchestra together.
'Father of the French symphony'. He founded the Concert des Amateurs and later handed its direction to Saint-Georges.
Opéra-comique: Tom Jones
The chessboard and the stave are one and the same.
My next move is to join you.
A composer and the strongest chess player of his day. He astonished London by playing three games at once blindfold. His Analyse du jeu des Échecs is regarded as a classic.
Piccinni: Didon
For tragic queens, no one surpasses me.
On your stage, I shall make Paris weep.
